findings.description: The single jq program that builds the row has several unguarded accesses that raise jq runtime errors instead of yielding null: ms() calls fromdateiso8601, which only accepts YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (a '+00:00' offset or an empty string in pipeline.json started/finished aborts); voices() indexes e.metadata.companion_voice.planned (a boolean/string companion_voice aborts); model_mismatches runs keys[] on models_used (an array there yields spurious '0: model 0 used' degraded reasons). Because ROW="$(jq ...)" runs under set -e, any such error exits the script with jq's status 5, outside the documented 0/1/2 contract, and no row is written for that run.
findings.failure_mode: One malformed-but-plausible field in pipeline.json or a dissent envelope silently drops the run from runs.jsonl; a batch runner that treats non-2 exits as transient may retry forever or miscount rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap fragile lookups: ms(ts) as (try (ts|...|fromdateiso8601*1000) catch null), voices() with (e.metadata.companion_voice | objects | .planned), models_used | objects // {} before keys[]; and trap jq failure explicitly (ROW=... || usage "row build failed for $RUN_ID").

findings.description: The writer and the --validate branch of the same script disagree on phase fields. The writer passes name, model_requested and models_used straight through from pipeline.json ({name, label, session_id, model_requested, models_used, ...}) with no defaults, while the validator requires name:string, model_requested:string and models_used:object. A phase that failed before any model call (infrastructure_error, cap_failure on launch) or a pipeline that recorded models_used: null produces a row that ablation-row.sh --validate then rejects with 'phases[i]: field models_used has type null'. Likewise verdict_accuracy is emitted as whatever grade.json holds (a string value fails the boolean|null rule).
findings.failure_mode: A runs.jsonl written entirely by this tool fails this tool's own validator on the first failed-phase row, so the batch validation step exits 1 and blocks reporting.
findings.suggested_fix: Default in the writer: name: (.name // .label // ""), model_requested: (.model_requested // ""), models_used: (.models_used // {}), and coerce verdict_accuracy to boolean|null; or relax the validator to strn/objn for those three fields.

findings.description: Every input is handed to jq as a single --argjson argv string: the whole MODELINV ledger ($MINV, wrapped per line with {line,row}), grade.json ($GRADE_JSON), pipeline.json, the manifest, both envelopes and the transcript write list. Linux caps one argv string at 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN). A long pipeline run with many Flatline hops, or a grade.json that embeds hidden-test output, exceeds that and exec fails with 'Argument list too long'.
findings.failure_mode: The script dies with exit 126 (not in the 0/1/2 contract) and no row is written, precisely on the largest and most expensive runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Write MINV/GRADE/envelopes to temp files and pass them with --slurpfile/--rawfile (jq reads files without an argv limit); keep --arg only for the small scalars.

findings.cross_file_justification: The regen_sandbox_manifest call added in execute-agent.sh changes the sandbox the cycle-129 run-arms.sh single-skill arms (review-recall/audit-recall) receive; lib/sandbox-mount.sh's header promises that path is extracted 'WITHOUT behaviour change'.
findings.description: In arm mode (every run-arms.sh trial sets LOA_EVAL_ARM, including baseline) execute-agent.sh now always runs regen_sandbox_manifest when .claude/ exists, so every single-skill sandbox gains or rewrites .claude/checksums.json, and arm_evidence gains manifest_sha256. That is a behaviour change for the cycle-129 path the lib header says is unchanged, and it means recall batches run before and after this commit are no longer the same treatment when the suite-level aggregate merges them. Separately, mount_prompt_surface is called with ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE=/dev/null, so the 'mount=skill:<s>|tree' evidence the lib contract promises never reaches executor.json arm_evidence.
findings.failure_mode: Cross-batch comparison in evals/results/arms/<suite>/STATUS.json silently mixes two sandbox shapes; audits of executor.json cannot tell which mount mode a run used.
findings.suggested_fix: Either gate regen on 'toggles actually modified .claude/' (non-empty ARM_TOGGLES) rather than ARM_MODE, or document the baseline change and bump a harness/arm-schema marker in the recall MANIFEST; and point mount_prompt_surface at $arm_ev_file so its evidence line is recorded.

findings.description: Two silent under/over-count paths in the cap check. (1) Ledger rows whose ts is not parseable by datetime.fromisoformat (an epoch number, a 7-digit fraction on Python <3.11, a missing ts) are skipped and only counted in 'skipped N malformed line(s)' on stderr; the total still prints as if complete, so a ledger with a different ts shape reports ledger_usd 0 against the cycle cap. (2) run-row dedup is first-seen-wins keyed on run_id: a run re-rowed (smoke row first, graded row with updated ledger_cost_usd later) keeps the stale cost, while rows with an empty run_id are never deduped and are counted twice when both runs.jsonl and a rows.jsonl hold them.
findings.failure_mode: The operator reads a headroom figure that is wrong in the unsafe direction with no non-zero exit to flag it.
findings.suggested_fix: Exit non-zero (or print 'INCOMPLETE') when skipped_lines > 0 or when a ledger has zero countable rows; for dedup prefer the last row per run_id (or the max cost_usd) and treat empty run_id as non-deduplicable but warn.

findings.description: Screen batches are excluded from the suite aggregate purely by directory name: find ... ! -path "$SUITE_DIR/screen-*". A normal batch an operator names --batch screen-foo is silently dropped from the aggregate, and the unquoted glob metacharacters in $SUITE_DIR (from --results-dir) can make the exclusion miss, letting screen batches into the aggregate. The STATUS.json already carries screen: true, which is the authoritative marker.
findings.failure_mode: Suite-level per_arm totals omit or include trials contrary to the bd-j4lwr rule, without any error.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the -path filter and exclude inside the jq reduce: map(select(.screen != true)); or reject --batch names starting with screen- when --screen is not set.

findings.description: compute_manifest lists files with find -type f, which excludes symlinks. A symlink added under tasks/ (or a task file replaced by a symlink to content outside the root) is not hashed, so freeze.sh writes a manifest that omits it and --check reports no drift for later changes to the link or its target. The frozen identity is therefore not a complete description of what validate-suite.sh and the runners will read.
findings.failure_mode: Suite content can change (via a symlink target) after the freeze while --check keeps returning 'OK'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use find "$d" \( -type f -o -type l \) and either refuse symlinks (die) or hash the link target path plus content; also assert no path contains a newline before hashing.
